significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both a form-(iii) law—“higher teacher competence predicts a larger novice penalty” and learner-state decodability predicts teaching effectiveness—and a form-(ii) mechanism in which the “learner-knowledge-level” representation causally controls explanation level and learning gain. This fixes expectations beyond the individual intervention: it predicts which topics and audiences will be taught poorly, links a pre-explanation internal quantity to later learning, and explains why adaptation succeeds; the emphasis on downstream learning is load-bearing given findings such as Bastani et al.'s “Generative AI Can Harm Learning” (PNAS, 2025), where assisted performance and subsequent unaided learning diverge. The claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal mechanism, while a comprehensive negative result would distinctly rule out the proposed curse, competence scaling, and learner-model gating rather than merely report a missing direction, although partial negatives would only prune parts of the composite account. The topic-substitution check passes: replacing these specific competence–penalty and representation–learning couplings with merely “investigate the relationship between language and AI intelligence” would not support this score.

reach.justification: The claim names three usable handles: the “learner-knowledge-level” probe, the corresponding steerable direction, and the “PREDICT-THEN-TEACH” design rule; the last is ex ante because the model infers the audience before producing the explanation, leaving an action window rather than merely diagnosing a completed failure. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction remains that stronger learner-state encoding forecasts greater learning and that novice-ward versus expert-ward movement produces ordered changes in explanation level and learner gain, so this is a transferable relation rather than only a procedure for searching for an arbitrary direction. The asserted scope spans model families and knowledge domains, with downstream uptake by people who design or deploy tutoring, patient-education, support, and training systems rather than only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. The topic-substitution check passes: the broad language-and-intelligence topic alone supplies none of these handles, lead time, transferable predictions, or deployment decisions.
